t: text

"I think you have already guessed the bitter truth, so I'm just going to dispel all remaining doubts. The Grand Experiment and the Cataclysm are one and the same!

Blinded by our pride, we searched for ways to increase our power. We found the Sources. We had no idea what the Seals were and why they were important. Every one of the Great Mages wanted only one thing - power, free power!

We tried to master the power of the Seals. When our first attempt failed, we continued to attack the Source Seal again and again with the most powerful spells until it cracked and released its power into the world. Power against power, you know? The Seals gave way, the world's shell cracked, and the Astral put an end to the Sarnaut as I knew it. You know the rest - the world in ruins, the legend of the Patrons, the Great Mages being the last stronghold of order in a realm of chaos... But I see that you don't believe my words.

I don't expect you to believe me. I wouldn't believe me either. But I have proof.

There's a cache in Yasker’s Tower. I doubt it has been discovered - I made sure it was difficult to find. Find a small bookshelf with an obscene word scratched into the side of it. Don't worry - I don't think anyone has been able to paint over it. Read it backwards, and the cache will open. Take the documents inside and do what you think is best with them. You can burn them - or you can publish them. But consider the consequences of your decision carefully. Remember: the future of the Empire depends on you!

The heroes took the papers to Mark Staritsin. He was shocked:

"Well, I'll be... This is huge! So the Great Mages have been lying to everyone for centuries? First, they almost destroyed our world, and now... What now? They are trapped on the pitiful pieces of land we know as the allods. Knowing they live forever... Indeed, their self-imposed punishment is a cruel one. Eternal imprisonment - and a voluntary one at that!

I guess it would've been better if you'd never found these records. They can divide the Empire and turn the people against Yasker and the other Great Mages... That would mean the end of this world! There would be no holding back the demon army!

I won't let that happen! For the Empire's sake, I'll take these papers from you and hide them in a deposit box in the deepest bunker. Trust me, that would be best. Knowledge is too dangerous, especially when it contradicts faith."

So you still had questions: who helped Tep gain divine power? Where did Klavdia go and why?
r156252.n: Ask what Nezeb said about the Grand Experiment

t: text

You haven't had enough? Shouldn't we stop here? Oh, well.

Before the heroes could recover from the shock after Klavdia's disappearance, the ghosts of Skrakan and Nezeb appeared before them! They had been imprisoned in Tep's Pyramid all this time...

You only had to question them...

This is what Nezeb said:

"Freedom! I'm finally free again! My body might be destroyed, but my spirit is stronger than ever!

Accursed Tep! Our Great Astral Campaign got us nowhere, and to make matters worse, we couldn't even die a proper death either. Years of captivity spent in that pyramid felt like an eternity to me!

Only dreams of revenge helped me hang onto my sanity. Every hour, every minute I'd dream of wiping the floor with the mad necromancer. Alas, my dreams were not destined to come true: a ghost's abilities are limited. I'll have to be satisfied with the fact that it was the Empire that took down my enemy.

I won't tell you my name. It was foolish and reckless to go along with Skrakan's crazy scheme. I'm disgraced by my ignominious and pointless death, but no one must know of my disgrace. To the Imperials, all who died in the astral campaign are heroes. Let it stay that way. The good of the Empire is above personal ambition!

But that's not what I want to talk to you about. I'm concerned about the Sources you know as the Seals.

While I was held in the Pyramid, I had plenty of time to think. After he got himself a new body, Tep would often taunt us, the bodiless ones. So I had enough food for thought. And some of my conclusions are disturbing.

I hope you're brave enough to challenge the forces that killed me. You and the other heroes are responsible for the future of our great realm. Honor the memory of those who gave their lives for the Empire!

Tep... I'm still amazed at the power in his madness. Who would have thought that one day the once-dead man would try to drag the whole world into oblivion?

It scares me how easily Tep dealt with his enemies. How easily he created a whole world, albeit an illusory one. If it's not divine power, then it's something very close to one. And I think I know what the secret of his incredible power is. It's the Seals!

I know that Tep experimented with a small fragment of one of the Seals and drew power from it to create his Plague. This is one of the manifestations of the Sources - the manifestation of death. But the Pyramid… Illusions, energy, matter, the creation of new life and the impact on the mind. A full set of powers available to the Great Mages, and on top of that, the most elaborate curses. No, I don't believe that Tep could achieve all this alone. Until recently, he was just a body howling in pain, stuck between life and death. I'm sure Tep had help! And it was someone who knows everything about our Great Experiment."
r156253.n: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in Tep's Pyramid

t: text

Ha-ha! You're just in time to share in my triumph! The world is full of imperfect creatures… Rotting flesh, and dead thoughts...

I was once loved. I was once hated. That world has long died, turned to dust. There's no one who can comprehend the greatness of my ideas. Only dust and bones are around me...

The centuries of pain have taught me to listen to the music of the Universe. I finally understand the brilliant plan of the Creator! Now that I'm as powerful as the gods, I can fulfill it!

Do you really think you can challenge someone who has absorbed the ocean of pain and tempered his spirit in it?

He who understands the essence of creation does not need this weak flesh!

Look into your future. Isn't it wonderful?

Living flesh is imperfect. You will see that yourselves!"

And once you gave a good thrashing to his first body, it started releasing Tep's Plague.

"That was foolish... My old body is still infected with my plague. And you just let it out!"

Fortunately for you, Klavdia showed up then:

"Hang on! I was able to cure the plague before, and I'll do it again!"

And the sorceress fought alongside you. Tep was seemingly defeated when suddenly multiple Sparks started filling him with power.

"I will take your Sparks, and they will shine, glorifying me!" the villain exclaimed, and then...

...then Klavdia intercepted his own Spark.

"You wouldn't dare! No!!

Tep's last words echoed through the hall.

"At last! I've been waiting for this for so long! A power equal to gods' might is now in my hands. It's mine! You hear that? Mine!

I'm sorry, but I'll have to leave you. Farewell, heroes! Greatness awaits!"

And the red-haired sorceress vanished, leaving the confused heroes behind. The end!

Do you see now why I don't like this story?
text

After some heroics, you managed to activate the elevator in the laboratory. You just had to go up.

I'll quote Klavdia here:

"All you have to do is to go up to the top of the Pyramid and fight Tep. The battle would be the stuff of legends! If someone lives to tell them, that is.

But I feel a sense of misgiving. The elevator is the only way to get to the top, which makes it the perfect place for an ambush. At least for your group. The enemy will probably strike as soon as you get there! So I'll go first and draw them away. I have my own tricks so I'll be there before you.

Oh, I almost forgot! Remember that three-headed thing at the ship graveyard? Tep has let his pet dragon loose - the one you fought earlier. And it might take an interest in the elevator as it moves up. So keep your eyes open - you never know where trouble might come from.

Alright, wish me luck. See you at the top of the Pyramid!

Oh, it's a pity that words cannot convey the beauty of the ensuing battle. Defeating this creature was far from easy. You had to be cunning and resourceful.

When you got to the top, you met Klavdia.

"It looks like I overestimated my powers. I didn't stand a chance!

Tep is smart. He knew I'd be the first to get here, so that ambush wasn't laid for you. They were waiting for me. He planned for that three-headed monster to destroy you when you were moving up. And he wanted to catch me alive! I dread to imagine what would've happened.

Oh... Everything hurts! With these injuries I can't help you in the next battle. You'll have to fight Tep without me..."
text

I'll quote Klavdia. She told you this in Tep's Pyramid:

"Does the name of Celestine de Ardeur mean anything to you? No? And she dreams of wreaking vengeance on you. Because of you, she became a cripple confined to the Pyramid forever.

That's Nihil. Yes, you fought her to save the mechanic Charles de Doucer. Yet I remember her as a young and enthusiastic elven girl. Simeon de Ardeur predicted a great future for her! Well, I guess it came true...

I think I know how Tep managed to win Celestine over. She'd always had an interest in machinery, so her thirst for knowledge outweighed her love for her House. She created Caesaria, the artificial intelligence controlling the Darkblood Citadel. And now Nihil has become an AI herself.

Tep has severely punished her for the defeat. Tep managed to return Nihil's spark into her dead body. He made her his loyal watchdog, damaged but still extremely dangerous. Tep has integrated the body of his disgraced servant into the control mechanisms of the Pyramid. She won't let anyone harm her brainchild. Can you imagine how she must be suffering. She no longer has any notion of the Beauty.

Please make her death as painless possible. I feel sorry for her. No one deserves this..."

So... You managed to defeat her and disable the mechanisms she controlled. This is how Klavdia reacted to her death:

"You wouldn't wish it on your worst enemy, being confined to your creation and having to watch as it gets destroyed...

Nihil can finally rest in peace... I wish I'd gotten through to her after our victory. Celestine's brilliant mind could have done so much for the Beauty that's so important to the Elves. But what's done cannot be undone. Now you should go to the enemy's den and eliminate this threat to the world."
text

What is insanity? They say insanity is doing the same thing over and over again. And expecting different results. If so, then Tep is clearly insane...

After all, he had to resurrect over and over again for thousands of years. Really, I could never understand why people are drawn to him... After all, only a madman can believe this maniac.

Do you know how Tep keeps his cultists? First, he promises them the world, eternal life, and all that. Then he demands an entrance fee and a monthly tax - part of the Spark's radiance. Finally, the newcomer is sent to recruit other unfortunates. Brought a new fool into the cult? Get a sip of his life. If you screwed up, you pay with your own. Such is Tep's Pyramid...
r156260.n: What is insanity? They say insanity is doing the same thing over and…

t: text

"All the words in the world can't express my gratitude. My friends found peace at last. The threat that was hanging over Umoir is gone. You did that. I can leave now.

We will never see each other again, so... Farewell. Fighting by your side was a great honor. While Sarnaut is under your protection, I'm not worried. My time is long gone. Your time is just beginning!" Those were Reniesta's parting words.

You reported back to Vseslav.

"The Demon is defeated?!

Praise you! And praise the ancestors! If it hadn't been for you, who knows what would've happened to Umoir. The whole world should hear about you. If you want that, I'll make it happen.

But I won't keep you. Great undertakings await you, I'm sure. We can defeat the remaining undead ourselves. Some are still wandering around. Which is understandable - who wants to spend an eternity in a damp grave?"

The Blight has lost its power since then. Slowly but surely it retreated from the Umoir lands. And the heroes have gone back to sleep in their tomb.
r156261.n: "All the words in the world can't express my gratitude. My friends…

t: text

You were standing on the ancient burial ground, feeling the cold of the dungeons. Before you were the old heroes of Sarnaut, now slaves to a ruthless demon.

"Here they come, the heroes of Sarnaut! Blind fools coming to meet their death!" said Fergard.

"This scum dares to challenge Sarn? Challenge us?!" exclaimed Danas in outrage.

"They want to lay with us in the dark tombs of the Burial Mound? How can we deny them?" said Naira snidely.

And a terrible battle began - with those who had once been the defenders of Sarnaut. They had already defeated the Demon, but now they fought on its side.

As soon as you defeated them, it appeared from its grave:

"Your victories mean nothing, and you are nothing. Servants of Shadow who call themselves warriors of Light! Keep holding onto your trinkets! They did not help these fools. Raise, you slaves! You are doomed to fight... forever!"

"We... obey. We are one!" Those were the words of the fallen heroes.

But even the Demon was unable to fight off your onslaught.

"Well... So be it. Enjoy your victory while you can. Live in your bloody world! I have eternity!" Sarn's Demon disappeared after that.
r156262.n: Ask about the battle with the Demon

t: text

The masks are discarded. The ghost turned out to be Reniesta, that “number 4 from Umoir”. The traitor whose name was forever tainted. The Demon and those he controlled were waiting ahead. I guess I'll let her speak:

"What's with the scroll and the cape, you ask? Tensess himself gave them to Skrakan. Why? For what purpose? I don’t know for sure. I suppose Tensess wanted to protect Skrakan during his experiment. But the Great Mage summoned an ancient demon to Umoir by mistake, and everything went pear-shaped. Animals turned into monsters, spirits went crazy... The Blight started then, do you understand? My friends stopped it. They defeated the demon and laid it to rest for all eternity.

At least that's what I thought... But then this stupid girl Catherina brought the damned thing back to life. And the whole thing started all over again. What's even worse, my friends, is that Danas, Fergard, and Naira were buried here together with their bitter enemy. The people of Umoir believed that this was the way to protect the dead from the corruption of demonic magic. That was a grievous mistake. Now the three of them will forever be the Demon's slaves.

I beg you to end their suffering. And be careful! They are experienced warriors, and it won't be easy to defeat them. Besides, the Demon has surely granted them a piece of his foul power. The scroll and the cape will help you in this battle. Use the scroll to break the connection between the heroes and the Demon. The cape will protect you from the deadliest attacks and spells.

Good luck! I will be praying for you... There's nothing else for me to do.

There was a glorious hero with us, Sir Brian. He was a paladin. His sword ended my life when I deceived my friends. His sword brought me back to life. Ancient magic works in mysterious ways..."
text

Ancient bird maidens. Once upon a time, there were many of them, but alas, all good things disappear with time. There are just a few of them left. It's fortunate that some of them are on Umoir... But is it really? One of them has fallen under the influence of the Blight...

It's sad. There is not enough beauty in this world...

I'll let our guide speak:

We are close to the center of the Mound, the Heroes' tombs. One last guard stands in our way...

Have you heard about the bird of sorrow, Sirin? Two mystical birds lived here, on Umoir. Sirin and Gamayun. They spent centuries in this place, and saw both glorious and dark days. Gamayun sang songs of happiness and joy, while Sirin sang about sweet sorrow and hard lessons taught by the past.

As time went by, there was more sorrow than joy. I couldn't understand what made Sirin hide in these catacombs, but then it hit me! It was Catherina who imprisoned her in this gloomy place. Sirin was meant to sing about all the evil deeds of the queen, and to predict the end of Umoir. Who would possibly enjoy listening to this?

Unfortunately, Sirin stayed here for too long. The Demon's influence corrupted her body and mind. Now her songs are full of poison, and all she sings about is pain and death. We must end her suffering.

The problem is, she could use this area to her advantage. If she manages to fly high, it will be hard to defeat her - she can easily kill you all from up there. Try using her poisonous slime on her...

All birds keep their feathers clean. If you smear them with her own slime, she will be distracted and won't fly up. She will furiously beat her wings, and that's when you must strike."

Well, Sirin was defeated. And her death led to some revelations from your ghostly helper:

Sirin was singing songs of sorrow and despair, peering into souls and digging up secrets. I can't do this anymore! I have a confession to make. There's something I've been hiding from you.

My name is Reniesta. I first came to Umoir with my sworn sister and brothers a long time ago. We were trying to find out what happened to the Great Mage Skrakan. We saw a lot. We walked along many roads together. We fought shoulder to shoulder...

After everything we'd been through, I betrayed them. Betrayed my friends, my allies! For what? For some scroll and cape!"
text

Ogres, trolls, cyclopes, giants...

Sarn created many strong creatures. Fortunately for you, most of them are rather dull. That's putting it mildly. The Turses were the most intelligent of them, but the Elves wiped them out.

But here's an example of rare stupidity:

"Our next enemy makes me want to gloat. The Demon resurrected a cyclops named Brainum the Third - I guess he'd considered himself an aristocrat or something. Anyway, the Demon wanted to add this giant monster to his army, but he miscalculated. Brainum's greed was as massive as his strength. He's in the treasury at the moment, and it doesn't look like he's leaving it any time soon.

Of course, we could leave him to the locals. There are plenty of them to overpower him. Unfortunately, the only way to the tombs is through the treasury, and we don't have enough time to wait while they do it for us. You'll have to defeat him yourselves.

Brainum was stupid when he was still alive. Now he has no brain at all. Don't turn your back to him. Just one blow, and you're a wet spot on the ground! My advise is to split and take up positions in different corners of the treasury. His attention will be divided, and he will be running around the room... crushing everything in his way and shooting a magic beam from his eye. Look around. You might find something that will help you pacify him...

There's another danger I want you to remember about. If Brainum gets really mad, he can crush rocks and stones! He can easily bring down the whole tomb with you inside it. Don't let him focus on one target. Keep distracting him."

We won't be analyzing the family trees of overgrown monsters. The first two Brainums were trolls, if I remember correctly.

And that's how that dynasty ended. This is what the sorceress said about that:

"Ogres, trolls, cyclopes... I find their endless stupidity somewhat charming. Just imagine what it would be like if Brainum had brains? You'd be in deep trouble.

The tombs are near. There's just the final obstacle..."
r156265.n: Tell me about Brainum the Third

t: text

Perhaps you and the others noticed that beliefs are different on the Kanian allods. The church spread its power throughout the Kanian Archipelago, and there's no other authority except the church on Forox, but it's not the same on Umoir. Maybe that's why there are so many sorcerers and witches here.

But we'll get back to it later. Let's talk about Morrana. That's what the ghost of that sorceress told you:

"When I was alive, I was a sorceress myself. I knew my limits, though, and I knew what I could do. Morrana is not like me...

Her powers are immense. Local peasants call her a Goddess of Death. She brought many woes upon these lands, poisoning the wells and killing the cattle with her plague. She might be more powerful than some of the Great Mages. I racked my brains over this whole thing for a while, but then it hit me.

The Scroll of Tensess! An ancient parchment inscribed with words of great power. I had a chance to see it during his lifetime... And let me tell you, many troubles happened because of this scroll, even if it bears the name of one of the best Great Mages. Morrana uses the magic contained in it to make her rituals more powerful. I don’t know where she got it and why she came to the Burial Mound with it. She probably wanted to enslave the Demon and become even stronger... She's so naive.

In any case, her arrival is a good thing for us. The scroll can come in handy in our fight against the Demon. I suggest we kill two birds with one stone - get the relic and save Sarnaut from this wicked witch. The secret to fighting mages of this level is to turn their sorcery against them. Carefully look around before the battle begins - is there anything around that can help us?

Morrana will surround herself with loyal servants. It's best to hit them with her own magic. But be careful - too much ancient magic can play a cruel trick on you."

Fortunately, even the Scroll of Tensess didn't help this witch.

"She's not the first one to fall because of her own arrogance. And not the last one. Whether fortunately or unfortunately, only time will show.

We're halfway through. The way to the inner chamber is open now. Keep your guard up: even I don't know what dangers lie ahead. Greatest warriors and most skillful mages are buried in these tombs. The Demon will surely summon them to its aid! On the other hand, not every creature it summons will obey it..."
text

This place attracts all kinds of vermin. The giant toad, ancient undead... And you haven't even reached the entrance yet! You want to know what happened next?

So, next enemy. That's what someone else said about it:

"Now it's time to face the most dreadful Blighted creature you can find on Umoir. To tell you the truth, it's not just the Blight that created it. It's a real magical conundrum.

Eye Stare is one of the oldest Treants in this place. Long ago it started dabbling in death magic, and its brethren exiled it to the Burial Mound. Which worked in its favor, because this place was exactly where it wanted to be. Plenty of dead bodies to raise, plenty of restless souls to let into its body. After a while, it lost its mind and decided it was the king of the local undead. When the Blight came, it readily accepted it, too. It became a loyal servant of the Demon. The locals were calling it Asura One Eye. Which doesn't tell you how terrifying it is. You'll see.

What really troubles me is its ability to turn invisible and attack from behind. It may invade your minds, so stay alert. Try using ashes from the urns here to reveal it when it's hidden, but be fast! The longer it stays disguised, the stronger it becomes.

Of course, Eye Stare also got itself some minions! It summoned the dead, and they answered its call. They can also become invisible, but luckily, ashes reveal them, too.

Do you understand now? This is where evil forces have been gathering.

It's a good thing you dealt with Eye Stare... You even got an interesting trophy.

"That's how Eye Stare keeps itself hidden! It had an ancient relic on it, a magical cape which I've seen before. Destiny's sense of humor is... peculiar.

Here's another joke. While you were fighting Eye Stare, guess who entered the Mound? Morrana herself. With the Scroll of Tensess in her hands! But first things first."
text

Interesting. The Blight is an incredible phenomenon. It's basically Life in a different form. It's too bad we can't coexist with it.

But there's a power that always opposes Life: Death. It's a good thing when your enemies help you defeat them. You don't understand?

Alright, let me tell you what that sorceress said:

"The monster maned Zomgie can raise the dead from their graves. It will be extremely difficult to defeat it since there's a huge cemetery around us. Thankfully, Blighted carnivorous plants don't like the living dead, so nature is going to be your ally in this fight against Death. It will distract the undead horde while you are fighting Zomgie.

So if you go through the Burial Grounds, you'll have to deal with Zomgie. Watch where it's looking. Its stare can be deadly."
text

Being crushed by a toad... Not the most heroic death. The Blight creates astonishing creatures...

That's what the ghost that accompanied you said:

"It was dangerous even before the Blight, and now it's a real monster. Its name speaks for itself. It jams you into the ground, crushing your bones and flesh. Beware of its mighty croaking, too. There's a terrifying power in its voice. If you can, don't let it croak at all. Do something to distract it.

The battle with Jam will be long and exhausting, but if you keep looking upwards, you will avoid getting killed."

Of course, you made it past Jam.
r156269.n: Being crushed by a toad... Not the most heroic death. The Blight…

t: text

What's our situation?

Vseslav with Catherina's minions stayed behind to guard the approaches. You, accompanied by the ghost of some strange sorceress, went into the depths.

You're probably wondering what happened next.

Well, first you had to decide which path to take. But perhaps I'll let this rebellious soul speak:

"The time has come. Before the Demon has a chance to raise a new army, we need to enter the tomb and challenge him! Your path lies through the thicket full of the undead. But that's not the worst part. There are only two ways to the tomb, and both of them are extremely dangerous.

One lies through the dead water. A huge ancient toad called Jam lives there.

The other road winds through the burial grounds where an ancient monster dwells. It once used to be a powerful necromancer. Tep was his name, I think... Oh, I see you know that name, don't you?

Choose your path wisely! And take this trinket. Use it to summon me at any time! I'll be with you all the time, unseen. I'll try and warn you if something is wrong. Best of luck to you!"

So what did you choose? Or maybe you defeated both enemies?
r156270.n: Yes, I want to know what happens at the Burial Mound.

t: text

"Let me warn you. Listen to what Skrakan says. He's the wisest one in the universe! Think about it: what is this endless journey of Klavdia's? Why is Sarn desperately trying to break free once again? What encouraged him, aside from his madness and his followers? Be on your guard.

I'm afraid the Blight soon might seem like the least of our worries. It's just another form of life that came to an unfamiliar world. The Blight is just trying to survive. Cut off from Sarn, it will leave now. We'll be left with bitter memories...

Go to Lovewise Catfish, tell him what I told you about gods and mortals. Let all others learn this lesson, too."

Lovewise heard you out and said,

"There's disquiet in the air...

Unbelievable...

This is the ultimate Creation! It's one thing to create a new allod, a lifeless piece of land - which is impressive on its own. But creating a new life? Sarn is amazing. Long ago, when he was still sane, his creations were truly beautiful.

Faith provides gods with power. Not only gods - common mortals, too. Faith and will are the key! We will not be able to comprehend this mystery until we dispel all doubt. It's thanks to you that Nezeb and Skrakan were able to come to your aid.

So, there is another truth that people are not ready to comprehend just yet. We ought to keep the scrolls with your stories in a bookcase, behind Aidenus's seal, and make sure it's more secure than the one holding Sarn..."
text

Of course, there was a conversation with Aidenus. The old man was concerned about the events.

"I've been waiting for your return. I had a feeling that something terrible was about to happen... But you are here, and everything's all right. We should thank you for saving us all again... And for the new kernels of truth, too.

I'm glad to see you safe and sound. Tell me exactly what happened. We have a lot to think about.

Poor Catherina...

I cannot imagine how miserable she must feel right now. Sarn tricked her, broke her spirit, turned her inside out and exposed her darkness to the whole world... But who is without sin? She's conceited and short-tempered, it's true, but all she cares about is order and justice! She's diligently seeking power all the time - that deserves respect!

We can't comprehend God's intentions. We, mages, tried once, and failed. Exactly. Catherina wanted to spread the faith in the Light in Umoir, make the locals believe in it - and in her as the Lightbringer. Believers and followers would have made her stronger. But she failed, too. There weren't too many loyal believers. However, you should remember: the more believers you have, the stronger your powers are. It may help you in very dangerous situations."
r156272.n: Tell me what I told Aidenus

t: text

"As for the faith, I have to mention that Catherina didn't enlist the demon's help from the start. Initially, she wanted to spread the power of the Light in Umoir, make the locals believe in it - and in her as the Lightbringer. Believers and followers would have made her stronger. I wonder if you succeeded because you'd gained a few followers, too? Remember all those who asked for your help. It raises a few questions, doesn't it?

I think we may let the public know what happened. Go to Mark Staritsyn and tell him whatever you feel like sharing. But let's keep Nezeb's words to ourselves."

Mark heard you out and said,

"Dark times are ahead... Get some rest before the Empire calls upon you again. You might not get the chance later.

The longer I know you, the more interesting stories I hear! But you know, I'm willing to believe every single word you say. To tell the truth, Yasker and the City Council do as well.

So, you've witnessed... what? The Creation? An allod appeared out of nowhere. But it didn't just appear - you helped create it. Now this mysterious Blight - a new life that influences other lives... Think about it - Sarn drew his power from his followers! It didn't matter who they were. They believed in him, and it granted him all these abilities.

I guess you made it possible for Nezeb and Skrakan to come to the rescue. Any creator may become god-like if their will is strong enough...

I feel sorry that I'll have to classify this information for the time being. But I will be waiting for news from you!"
text

Of course, there was a conversation with Yasker. The leader of the Empire was alarmed by the events.

"I can feel that something important happened far away in the Astral. I can't tell you how I know it. Let's just say I didn't sleep well last night.

Hm. I can also see that I shouldn't worry too much. I suppose I can congratulate you on the successful completion of your mission. No need to draw up a report - I don't think this situation needs any extra paperwork.

However, I'm asking you to tell me what happened in detail...

Oh, so that's how it went down...

Do you remember how it all began? A backwater harbor in Eljune, pirates and their unreliable information... Chasing after Klavdia... What an interesting person, by the way. Wherever she goes, all kinds of dangerous things follow her. And her enthusiastic speeches about Nihaz's power and what she can do with it... It's suspicious. Quite suspicious.

I don't like Nezeb's words either. He's not one to beat about the bush. What's changed? It looks like there won't be peace in Sarnaut - it will continue to tear itself apart. Just think about it! The Blight is one of Sarn's creations. Which means it has the right to exist in this world, just like we do. The problem is, we couldn't coexist. If his plans worked, our war with the League would have felt like a children's game in comparison. And it still might... We shouldn't toy with divine powers.

In this respect, I'm not that surprised by Catherina's madness. Frankly speaking, I don't understand how she managed to join the Conclave back then. She should keep ruling Umoir and forget about everything else. Now that the Veil is lifted, our hands are free. We may begin our operation! On behalf of the Empire, I commend you for the successful completion of this mission. However, I never doubted that you could handle it."
r156274.n: Tell me what I told Yasker

t: text

She told you where the Blight came from:

"The Blight? The Blight is just another side of creation. It's another form of life made of the same primal matter. The only difference is that it's able to corrupt other forms of life. Sarn has gone mad. His gift of the Creation now serves evil, translating its wicked fantasies into reality.

While my mind was under his control, I could touch his consciousness... But I was too afraid. What I'd glimpsed was enough to keep me away. It's an ocean of madness and malice... Well, now I sound like that crazy old man Tale Teller.

It's unimaginable. Just one little shard of Sarn's soul in the avatar he created - and it holds immense power. He could have done so much with this power, but he's wasting it on his attempts to break free... You know, I think I almost pity him. I didn't know I had it in me..."

And this is where you ended up:

"This is the Seal. If only you could sense all the real, primal magic that surrounds us here! It's everywhere. If only you could understand how tempting it is... but I won't dare touch it. I've learned my lesson. Nihaz, who created the Seals, was way stronger and craftier than Sarn. Oh, if the God of Light tried to be like him, we can only wonder what the God of Darkness was capable of.

We'd better leave this place.  It's not good for mortal beings."
r156276.n: She told you where the Blight came from: "The Blight? The Blight is…

t: text

She told you how Sarn had been able to control her.

"It wasn't Sarn - I outwitted myself. I was looking for a source of power, so I studied Skrakan's archives. He described a strange event in Gorluxor's Tower, when a strong demon appeared out of nowhere. There was so much I could do with this kind of power! Incredible magic and advanced technology! I could bring peace to the world, establish order and justice!

Except it wasn't just a random demon. It was one of the first children of Sarn, his own Avatar created during the time of the Curse. I thought I was controlling him, but he was slowly taking over my consciousness. That's how I unwittingly helped spread the Blight. Or rather, I failed to stop it from spreading."
r156277.n: She told you how Sarn had been able to control her. "It wasn't Sarn -…

t: text

Now you needed to question Catherina about everything she knew. The events took her down a peg.

When she asked you about Skrakan and Nezeb, she'd already had a theory.

"This is an interesting story. You first met their Sparks in Tep's Pyramid. And here they materialized.

I guess you had a hand in it. You've seen divine forces at work. You've learned about the mystery of Creation. The Astral here is malleable like potter's clay - and anyone who knows how to handle it can use it for their own purposes. But you say you don't know anything about it... In that case, let's call it a spark of genius. You needed allies, and they answered your call. Your willpower combined with Sarn's power... This is the result.

You don't have to worry about the consequences. As soon as you leave this place, they will disappear. Simple as that."
r156278.n: Tell me about the aftermath of the events on the Eclipse

t: text

Sarn joined the battle again. He kept trying to break free.

"Why did you betray me? I could have created a new, more beautiful world for you. But you chose death... So be it! What wonderful, fierce people I created! Go on, attack me! It will only make me stronger! I used to give gifts to people. Now I only have curses! This pathetic Seal can't hold me! Die! Perish! Cease to exist! Freedom is so close!

You are my best creation. The best destroyers in all the worlds! You have fulfilled your purpose. This. Is. The end.

So the battle began on the surface of one of the Seals. Sarn did everything he could to destroy it, but... this attempt to break free was unsuccessful. He was defeated once again:

"What did I create...? What has become of you...? How could you... surpass... me?"
r156279.n: Sarn joined the battle again. He kept trying to break free. "Why did…

t: text

Harat was consumed by power which turned him into an Elemental of fire and darkness.

"So Catherina managed to capture not one but two dragons! I heard the rumors but didn't quite believe them. Who could have known...

There is no time to dwell on how she did it. Our enemy has a powerful weapon in their hands. The power of the dragons! And now the world is in great danger.

Hold on to your weapons - this will be a difficult battle!" warned Anton Turischev.

Harat didn't hide his elation:

"The pain... The pleasure... The power! I am even stronger than dragons. I will destroy the Seal and free Sarn! Witness the greatest sorcery in the history of Sarnaut... The ultimate sorcery!

May the ritual begin!"

That battle was indescribable. In addition to battling Harat, you had to keep an eye on Catherina so she wouldn't open the Seal.

"You will never defeat me... I will never die... And you will never resurrect! You could hardly defeat my shadow! What do you hope to accomplish?! Even my shadow nearly killed you. Why do you keep fighting? You're doomed! Why prolong your suffering? Are you trying to interfere with the Queen's plans?

I'm... fading... It doesn't matter. This ship is an arrow fired at the heart of the world. And it reached its target! The ritual... can't... be stopped..." Even though Harat was defeated, the world was still on the brink of destruction.
r156282.n: Harat was consumed by power which turned him into an Elemental of fire…

t: text

Catherina's most terrifying weapon. That's what Anton Turischev said when he saw it:

"We're close. I can see the force field protecting... Wait, could this be...? Dragons!

But how? What are they doing here, on the Eclipse? Are they the "keys" to the Seals that will destroy Sarnaut? If so, they have to be eliminated!

How did Catherina capture the Dragons? You sure know which questions to ask. I'm no authority here, but I suspect someone very powerful helped her. You can be thrice gifted but only your wits can save you when you're facing a dragon.

Honestly, that sudden betrayal makes no sense to me. Even if she acts like a petulant child sometimes, she has a good head on her shoulders. I don't know why she would need to capture dragons. This whole business smells bad. And my intuition can be trusted.

Those dragons were Soliskar the Wise and Agrus the Callous... And their captor was the famous hunter Harat.

"Are you here to take a look at my pets? The world has never seen a creature as perfect as a dragon. It would pain me to sacrifice them. I wish there was another way to break the Seal and set the Creator free. However, this is none of your business. They won't even have you for breakfast, you bunch of traitors!

What's wrong? You're not fleeing? Are you really going to fight two dragons? Ha ha ha!"

Few can handle even one dragon. But two? Not easy at all...

As soon as you defeated the dragons, Harat took their powers, leaving their unconscious bodies behind.

Oh the Brightest, grant me fire!

Oh the Darkest, send down the darkness!

Let the earth and the skies burn! Let the Astral flare!

Give me everything you have! Bright flame, pitch darkness! More power! More! Mor..."
text

Mechos, a strange creature that looked like it was made from pieces of the Construct. An alien creature that appeared out of nowhere.

It's still a mystery.

"That dreadful thing! No, it didn't come from our shipyard, I'd stake my life on it. Have you ever encountered anything like it? Me neither.

It's like an enemy force has taken control of our construct. It looks so strange... So static, neat, and unwavering. And it fights strangely, too. Not like Catherina's fighters. They are driven mostly by fury, but this is a cold and ruthless killer. And you know what? I've visited the Astral more times than I can count, but I've never seen the likes of it. If I didn’t know it used to be the construct, I would say it came from another world...

Whatever it was, it's dead now. And we have to keep going!" said Anton Turischev.

Oh, there was a reason for that premonition...
text

There was a valiant captain who traveled the world...

Why just captain? Catherina's crew is quite big. Her loyal apprentice was among the defenders of the ship: Zarida Zharova. Remember this name! Because she won't forget her defeat...

Anyway, you managed to get aboard the ship. Captain Ignat Krivov. Catherina's loyal dog...

Anton Turischev will narrate the story:

"So, the upper deck. That’s a good decision. There's more space, so it's easier to fight. However, we will be exposed. Catherina will send her dogs after us. Most of all, I'm scared of Captain Krivov. He once drunkenly boasted that he can rip anyone apart thanks to his "new suit".

And the man means what he says. I hear Catherina armed him with a weapon that no one has seen before. So beware. If you run into Ignat, you'll have to fight!

Of course, Krivov had something to say as well:

"Landlubbers! How dare you climb aboard my darling Eclipse! I'm going to hang you all from the yardarm! I swear! Let my crew laugh while you squirm!

Do you think you're heroes? Yeah?! You got a drop of power, joined with some heretics and traitors, and now you think you're strong enough to defeat our Queen's army? Hah! The Queen has planned for this! She has planned for everything! Yes!

You know what technology is? It is order. Absolute order. No mistakes made or forgiven. I will teach you this lesson... Yes!"

Oh, that order of theirs... Listen to him. It's not just rambling of an old drunkard. As soon as you defeated Krivov and his construct...
r156285.n: Tell me about Captain Ignat Krivov

t: text

"Oh! I thought ghosts couldn't feel a thing... no heat, no pain. But I'm definitely feeling both. Am I alive?

Oh wait! I remember you! You released my spirit from under Tep’s control, and I told you the truth about the cataclysm!

So now I'm alive? I came back to life? It's not possible! I have to be dead! Do you understand? Dead! My mistake caused so many deaths. They’re all dead, but I'm alive. This... This is painful. Why did you bring me back? I made so many mistakes. Why do you need me, a failure who died because of his foolishness?

The deeper the Astral, the easier it is to affect it. But you are not strong enough to create life from astral matter on your own. Not even Great Mages can do that. It's something only divine power, or something close to it, can accomplish. So someone helped you bring the old fool back to this wonderful world. And there is a reason for it, I imagine? Tell me more before I turn to ashes again. Hurry.

Oh, Catherina, Catherina... Your pride will be your undoing! No, I don't think she made this decision on her own. Breaking a Seal! It's unthinkable! Nobody can survive it, and Catherina is not suicidal. And she’s rather weak-willed, so I’m sure there is someone behind this.

You absolutely can't kill Catherina! Don’t even think about it! Killing a Great Mage near a Seal will break it for sure, and we will all be doomed. We need to neutralize her somehow before she does something we can't undo...

At any rate, it's time to act. There's no point in guessing. We have to stop her. Let's go!"
text

He he. So, the reactor... You really want to know? Well, then. Let's see. It's kind of your fault, you know. You don't agree?

I'll explain. Or rather, I'll quote Turischev:

"Okay, we're done with the goblins, and now there's no one to fix the reactor which we need to destroy in order to stop the Eclipse. It’s just that I’m afraid - Catherina's reactor is quite unusual! Do you really think the Queen needs Firebird to cure the Blight? Well, for that, too. But mostly as an energy source. The core of the reactor. If we manage to destroy the reactor and let the Firebird out, an ocean of energy will be released! I think the gift Klavdia gave you could probably be useful in a situation like this.

And there's another thing... During the fight, the goblins kept yelling something about a demon. Can Catherina control demons now? It's a terrifying thought - imagine what she might be capable of..."

Do you understand now? You gave Catherina the ability to reach the deeper layers of the Astral! But it's not that simple...

Yes, they were yelling about a demon for a reason. The reactor itself was the "demon" connected to the energy systems of the ship. So this combination of the demon and Firebird led to unexpected results and incredible efficiency.

It's hard to describe that battle. I can say that you defeated the creature, but only just. And the Firebird helped... But is it enough to paint a picture of what happened? I hope you'll see it yourself some day.

But what did you do after the victory? Toss a coin... and see Skrakan in his physical form...
r156287.n: Tell me about the reactor of the Eclipse

t: text

Have you ever wondered why every ship has those three mechanics? Goblin Tinkerer, Goblin Mechanic, and Goblin Repairman? Are those their actual names? I think those might be ranks in their hierarchy. What do we know about the Goblins? Not much!

The Eclipse is a large ship with a big crew. They had their own goblin repairmen. She really knew how to pick them.

Let our expert on the Astral speak:

"Cargo hold! That’s a good decision. They'll have a hard time catching us! The only thing they can do is crowd in on us...

But I'm only worried about those three mechanics. You might think they are as timid as goblins on most ships, but the crew of the Eclipse is unlike any other. They’re real animals who can bite through an iron wrench! And their machinery is just as annoying. They know the cargo hold in and out!"

Defeating the goblins was harder than anything else. But you did it!

"Well, I'll be damned. If all goblins were like these three, we wouldn't have Goblinball, because goblins would be using orcs as balls!" said Anton Turischev.
r156288.n: Have you ever wondered why every ship has those three mechanics?…

t: text

Is it good that the Eclipse is such a big cruiser? If this ship was fast and highly maneuverable, would you have caught up with it? But Catherina likes big... Ahem... Boats!

Of course, the Octulhu delayed you, but you still managed to catch up with the Eclipse. Now it was time to heroically board it. Fortunately, you are a person of reckless courage. A real daredevil!

Perhaps I will quote another hero of this story. The one and only. Anton Turischev, astral scientist and your faithful companion in this adventure! Can't leave him out:

"See, that's the Eclipse over there! It's going to be a good fight.

First, we’ll have to break through the shields of the Eclipse. The enemy crew will try and take out our cannoneers. While the shields are up, the traitor’s ship is completely invulnerable. Once they are down, we can use boarding bridges to get to the deck of the Eclipse. Pray that no one falls into the Astral! Don’t even think of jumping over. The Eclipse’s defense devices will kill you instantly. Use the bridges, there's no other way. Then we might have a chance.

Ready? Let's board it!"

So the fight began. Catherina personally organized a warm welcome. Oh, if this sorceress had been casting spells instead of swearing at you, the outcome would have been completely different! It would've been tragic. But even her obsession with Sarn couldn't change this proud woman. She took your boarding as a personal insult and tried to do everything in her power to keep you from breaking through the shields and getting aboard her ship.

Oh, what a fight... In the end, Catherina spat at you and retired to their chambers. The Eclipse was approaching its destination, and she was certain that her servants would stop you before you could get to her.

But you had to make another choice. Anton Turischev described this as well:

"Phew, we did it!

I’ve never been so scared in my life... I just wanted to jump into the Astral - it would've been a quick and painless death. But we did it! We broke through!

The Eclipse is way too large for us to split. They would easily take us out one by one, so we need to decide how we're going to get to the control room. There are two paths: through the upper deck where we'd run into Catherina’s servants, or through the cargo hold where we’ll have to destroy the reactor. Without it, the Eclipse will no longer be a threat. After that, we’ll deal with Catherina. The decision is up to you!"

If you chose the deck, then a meeting with Ignat Krivov awaited you. If you went through the hold - then it's a date with three goblins.
r156289.n: Is it good that the Eclipse is such a big cruiser? If this ship was…

t: text

Did anyone think traveling through the boundless Astral would be safe? Especially if you dived into its deepest layers?

In the depths, the most amazing creatures are waiting for unwary travelers.

Death is one of them. Sarn began creating his army of demons immediately after the onset of the Astral Era. The Octulhus are one of the main forces of his army. These creatures were going to destroy entire allods. And she was one of the first Octulhus he created.

Legends of especially dangerous creatures have been around for a long time - astral merchants in ports tell stories of how they barely escaped with their lives, and demon hunters describe how they harpooned a particularly powerful specimen, but the rope broke.

But I'm sure about one thing - few survived an encounter with Death.

I'm glad you were one of them. Defeating the Octulhu Progenitor is quite the feat!
r156290.n: Did anyone think traveling through the boundless Astral would be safe?…

t: text

Oh, those knights. Catherina's mechanical guards!

After your encounters with Tep's Mechanoids, you're probably wondering what they have in common with this marvel. Well... I'll put it this way: if they're not brothers, then at least they're cousins.

It all started with the Junes and their unforgettable golems. The Junes were the first to design all kinds of equipment.

The Hickuts got some samples, but they could not really understand where the source of energy was, what kind of batteries they used, and how these things worked in general. They had to invent a wheel, even though they learned the basics from the Junes.

Then the Kanians found the June golems. They played with them for a bit but got tired quickly. They didn't get anywhere, but there was one enthusiast among them. The name of this Great Mage was Smaragd. Through trial and error, he created something - more for fun than for function.

But Smaragd had an apprentice - it was Catherina.

By then, a technological revolution happened. The Arisen invented astral power engineering, the Elves successfully stole it from them, adding a lot of their own. Catherina contacted the Free Traders, picked up ideas here and there, and with the help of the Death Plant, she created this.

Powered by the Spark, this Knight is also sentient. And the guard of the Pier had magical abilities on top of everything else. There had to be a reason so many Umoir nobles perished in Catherina's dungeons. It looks like one of the local noble mages got here before us.

It was difficult, but you defeated him. All that remained was to follow the Eclipse.

I will quote Klavdia who had to stay on the pier:

"The distance between us and the Eclipse is increasing every second! Let’s not waste time!

I wish I could go with you. The Great Mage escaped, and the local gods cannot go to the Astral, because they are part of this world.  I’m the only one who can protect this allod until you come back. And if you don’t... Umoir is doomed. The fate of this world is really in your hands.

However, I can't let you go on your own. See this coin? No, don't make that face. It’s got the League national emblem on one side, and Imperial one the other. Remember what I told you about faith? Faith is power. People believe in their factions more than anything else! This very faith will help you.

Find a mighty source of power - it can be a ship reactor, for instance - and toss a coin there. Help will arrive immediately.

Enough talking! Board the ship!"
r156291.n: Oh, those knights. Catherina's mechanical guards! After your…

t: text

So, where were we? Perhaps, while traveling through these islands of Umoir, you have forgotten how it all began...

During the final battle with Tep, Klavdia Kalugina captured his Spark and then disappeared. The leaders of the League and the Empire, concerned about this, sent you after Klavdia.

The trail led you right here, to the League allod Umoir which was controlled by the Great Sorceress Catherina. Umoir is afflicted by a strange disease - the Blight which infects both animals and plants, turning them into monsters. In addition, Catherina is in conflict with adherents of old beliefs, trying to spread faith in the Light.

You managed to find out the following:

First, Klavdia used the power of Tep's Spark to establish her cult and faith in her as a protector. She's trying to gain as much power as possible. Did you really think she was bad? Tsk tsk!

Second, the Old Gods of Umoir really exist, and their power also depends on faith in them.

Third, some incomprehensible threat is approaching, and even the gods fear it.

In the end, you managed to reconcile the adherents of the old and new faith. However, the moment it happened, you were attacked by demons. In addition, the doors of Catherina's tower closed, and her guards began to attack anyone who tried to enter. After you finally managed to get into the tower, an unpleasant surprise awaited you there.

I have to retell the story once again...

"Catherina serves Sarn who created the Blight. There's no doubt about it. I do not care whether is was a conscious decision or not, but that doesn't matter. What matters is that the Eclipse is about to sail off to the heart of the world where Sarn is imprisoned. And I don't think it's a social visit! I'm sure she has keys to the Seals. Maybe not all of them, but even one broken Seal would be enough. My father is far away from this world, so no one would be able to stop the Prisoner. If he breaks free, Sarnaut is doomed!"

Of course, you had to follow her! Follow Catherina!
r156292.n: Yes, I want to know what will happen if I go after the Eclipse.

t: text

This fight did not decide the fate of the world. But it was important for your expedition. After covering the rear, you could move on. All you had to do was get past the ice barrier in the cave.

And the Tungars, now led by Tyk, Myk and Pyk, have become your friends. For the most part. Of course, there were other tribes who dreamed of the "upper world"... They left when an opportunity presented itself...

Since such conversations usually end with discussions about the fate of the world and the secrets of the universe, why break the tradition?

I'll give you a hint.

What did you see? On the bottom of the lake? A mysterious meteorite shard? We'll talk about that later.

Besides, perhaps you were curious about the fact that the Pridens came here from their homeland, Howlem. Let me tell you another fact: Ferris and Howlem have a number of common endemics. That is, creatures that live only there.

And one last observation - to the west of here, in Dragon Bay, there is a skeleton of a Great Dragon.

You see what I'm getting at?
r156293.n: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Tungar Camp

t: text

Well, you already know the power of faith. Imagine this: at the dawn of this world, there were almost no deities here. The first appeared when the energies of Creation, spread by Sarn, gave rise to anomalies that manifested in the form of the first elementals. But the power of faith made them real gods! Primitive tribes prayed to their idols, and that made them stronger.

We have a typical example. I don’t even know if some kind of spirit possessed the mammoth, or the mammoth became something else...

That's what a Priden said:

"That creature the Tungars worship actually exists, eysh! The ancient beast dwells in one of the deepest Northern caves. Myk told me they call it Toros.

Ay-hya... I took it for a regular old mammoth at first. But the body of this beast is obviously possessed by some hunhurr, eysh! It can control the power of cold and wind. The Tungars bring it offerings. They believe it will help it live forever, and it will annihilate all their enemies. And you know what the power of faith can do, don't you?

You will have to eliminate not only the mammoth, but also that crazy Tungar cult. Tyk, Pyk, and even Myk have agreed to help you, even though the thought of facing Toros scares them to death. Follow their example! Be brave and slay the monster!

Ferris has never seen a hunt like that, eysh!"

The fight was difficult, but you won.

"We all felt its death. Can you feel that, too, zoor? As if it has become warmer. And brrighter. And I can breathe more freely. What if it was actually... a god? Or something like that. It's a shame we will never find out.

But I'm happy that Toros is gone. That's one less threat, eysh!"
r156294.n: Tell me about the ancient mammoth Toros

t: text

The Tribe Chief Booka-Booka. It's a funny name. But that savage is far from funny. Riding on his stinking yak, he is formidable primarily because he can gather a huge crowd under his command.

I'll let our scout speak:

"It's about time we beheaded the most stubborn Tungar on this allod. As I expected, Chief Booka-Booka is not as revered as he used to be. Tyk and Pyk consider you their leader, for example. Together with Myk, they will help you in this fight. You probably understand that their help is worth a lot.

Still, be careful. Booka is a really strong enemy, eysh! He is brave and daring, like a bird that protects its nest from a lynx. When he was young, he tamed and saddled a wild yak by himself! You know, the Tungars are terrified of yaks. And as far as I know, he killed the previous chief and rightfully took his place. Such are their traditions!

I doubt you can take him alive. This hunhurr definitely won't be asking for mercy."

That's the way they are. Eysh!

Don't worry. That Tungar was strong, but you and your allies defeated him.

"Excellent, eysh! The Tungars will finally get off our back without their barking chief. Things will get better now. Of course, little groups of crazy fanatics will keep attacking us from time to time, but we'll have no trouble fighting them off.

But no more games. Our next enemy will be more serious."

Those were Maas-Tyna's words.
r156295.n: Tell me about the Chief Booka-Booka

t: text

Tyk is the best warrior, Pyk is the best hunter, and Myk is the best shaman.

Let's hear Maas-Tyna the Light-Footed:

"Believe it or not, there are decent warriors among the Tungars, eysh! They will try to duel you, and they will fight till their last gasp. They are the last hope of these savages. All Tungars are now hiding behind their champions.

They know you are coming, and they are ready to face you. The best warrior, the best hunter, and the best shaman. Defeat them - and the Tungars will scatter in terror! Will you do that?

But don't kill them, no! Show mercy. The spirits say those champions might turn out to be useful. A true hunter doesn't spill blood needlessly!"

And she's right. Don't try to take someone else's life. Don't do anything you can't fix later.

After you defeated them, these champions defected to you. I told you they respect strength. You managed to prove that you are stronger.
r156296.n: Tell me about the Tungar champions

t: text

You are not dealing with mad gods or feisty sorceresses this time! You are on the forgotten Ferris, where the Tungars live in the ice. These savages worship their barbarian deities. Strength is the only thing they respect.

You managed to piss them off. You captured their camp, insulted their deities, and beat up their leader. They can't wait to pay you back. Alas, the Historians are no match for you, and as soon as you leave the camp, it will be defenseless. And if the Tungars break in here, they will slaughter everyone.

The solution: strike first. Go to their camp and deal with them.
r156297.n: Yes, I want to know what happens in the Tungar Camp

t: text

Well, I guess it's time to go back to Umoir and talk to our old acquaintance:

"What brings you to my chambers? Are you here to boast about your triumph and gloat over my failure?

Where did you get this crystal?! Give it to me, I must... Oh, sorry! I'm still a little out of it after the whole Blight business.

Yes, I know something about this crystal. Long ago, I saw a shard like this one. It was about the size of my pinkie. The man who gave it to me said he'd found it on a wrecked ship covered in dead bodies of the Zem. I suppose those were Tep's followers - the Arisen who believed in the Light would have resurrected after death.

My research showed that the stone was emitting an unidentified energy. Its power was so strong that it suppressed and altered all other known magical fields. I tried but couldn't find a use for it, so in the end it became a part of the battery backup circuit for one of my mechanism. That device is still on the Eclipse... Oh, wait, you destroyed it when you were fighting my loyal captain Krivov!

I'm sorry, there is nothing else I can do. Captain Krivov is dead, and all my scientific research has turned to a pile of scrap metal, all thanks to you. No, no, I'm not blaming you - back then I wasn't myself. I didn't know what I was doing when I brought the world to the brink of destruction. But I can't help you now either.

If you don't mind, I will keep the shard and continue my research. If this is how it affects both living flesh and metal, I need to find a way to use it to battle the Blight. What if it's our only chance?!"
r156298.n: Ask what Catherina thinks about the crystal

t: text

Herbert was skeptical:

"A crystal as a source of mutation? That's not possible!

Yes, I can sense that it radiates some energy, but I don't understand its nature. If it's magic, then it's really unusual. But I have no doubt that this crystal was extracted from the meteorite at the bottom of the lake and transported to the Bestiary. What does that tell us? Two things!

First, the crystal was the key element of the scientists' research. Perhaps constant exposure to its radiation caused unexpected results.

Second, we don't know whether the experiment was successful or not. The Bestiary was abandoned a long time ago, and we don't know if the mutation was created on purpose or it was a side effect.

You know... I think you should speak with someone who knows more about technology and magic than anyone else in Sarnaut. Besides, they owe you their life. Can you guess who they are? The Great Sorceress Catherina!

t: text

Ooh, we're getting close to the source of all evil. You've already rescued Zimina from that creature - now you need to save the entire Ferris.

I'll repeat what Sergey Dozorin said:

"You know, I remember what you told me about your vision... And I've come to realize that you saw the heart of the mutation. Though you probably don't remember that.

There is a dead zone in the far end of the Bestiary. Animals and birds keep away from it. My dog refuses to go there, and honestly, I don't really want to myself. But I don't have a choice...

There must be a cave deep inside the complex. Whatever is in there, it holds answers to our questions. You will have to fight the thing that has destroyed the whole Bestiary. I've already called the technicians of the expedition - they are bringing all the necessary gear: hovering platforms, turrets, explosives... So you will also have to keep the staff and the equipment safe!

But don't be sad. Responsibility means trust, right? Just try not to die in there, alright? I'm sure we will need you help in the future. Good luck!"

Yes! That icy worm is dead! The story of the Bestiary would have ended there, but an unexpected discovery shed light on an old mystery.

"A crystal? A single stone drove all the animals in the area mad and turned them into monsters? Damn...

Well, I will leave this mystery to someone else. Baxter and I have better things to do. I'll go find the Prowls. I could do with a cup of their famous brew.

You really are good! I've heard a lot about you. But you know how people are - you can't believe everything you hear. Now I'm wondering who should be feared more, those defeated monsters... or you? Hmm.

Never mind.  It's time for a drink!

"So, our ways are parting. You need to go with the expedition, and I'm staying in the Bestiary. It's more peaceful here. And just I like the place, you know.

The most interesting things must be waiting for you in the heart of Ferris! Stick with Herbert. He is a smart and capable guy. You can rely on him in any situation!" said the brave hunter and bid you farewell. Now you need to show the crystal to the Surveyors.
text

As I said, more and more altered creatures were waiting for you. I still marvel at the carelessness of the Imperial scientists. In their pursuit of scientific discovery, they were willing to perform the most irresponsible and risky experiments. The League's Catherina is the same. So you can't help but wonder - is it the gods that are a threat to the world? Or is it us?

This is what the jaeger said:

"Remember how the Tungars were scared of yaks? Taming and driving the poor animal mad is the greatest feat for them. I'd like to see how they deal with an experimental specimen from the Bestiary. Yes, yes. Our precursors experimented even on yaks!

I managed to get into the archives of the Bestiary and found something about the research that was conducted in the year of the incident. The documents are surprisingly well-preserved and, most importantly, sorted into categories. Meet your enemy - the Thunderer project. It's an attempt to turn a yak into an energy-producing machine. According to the documents, the attempt failed. But I've seen the yak with my own eyes just recently. Even in the turbulent sectors of the Astral, I've never seen so many lightning bolts that illuminated the area around the creature. That's energy, isn't it?

I think that the mutation somehow affected its abilities.

I wonder if the mutation was accidental, or those scientists actually found a way to engineer it. Anyway, we will have to kill the monster before it becomes too dangerous."

Victory! Why are you surprised? Did you want to keep going?

"I wonder if one can dodge a lightning bolt. Can you try? Please?

"Well... That Thunderer is an interesting individual for sure. My ears are still ringing!

We are on the right track. Baxter refuses to keep moving, and he's a smart dog, if timid. And I can feel that we're close to the source of the mysterious disease."
text

Well, you took your first steps inside the Bestiary. The real surprises were still waiting for you. What's important is how the local fauna was changing...

It's not the first time it has occurred. Of course, it never happened on Sarnaut. A certain mind was behind these changes. A mind that was obsessed with order. Absolute, perfect order.

And there was an unusual kitty waiting for you...

"How much do you rely on your eyes? Jaegers are taught that your ears and nose are as important as your eyes. I still need Baxter to sniff things out for me, because the human sense of smell isn't nearly as strong. No, don't whine, buddy! Ah, this dog is too smart...

Alright. The deeper we go, the worse it gets. All animals inside the Bestiary seem to be covered with some sort of stone crust. Many of them are already dead, but the survivors... have turned into real monsters. Take that huge cougar. It keeps prowling around the complex and sniffing the air. A strange behavior, isn't it? That's what I thought so I decided to observe it quietly. And I realized that it had gone completely blind because of the mutation, so it relies on its hearing and sense of smell. You think it makes it weaker? Oh, no. It sees with its ears and nose just fine! And it's a problem for us! I barely managed to trick it so it couldn't hear me as I ran away.

But we can't keep tricking it forever. If you want to get deeper into the complex, you need to deal with it first. Or else we'd be ambushed at the most inopportune moment."

That's what we deal with here. There'll be more of them up ahead. Even if Rustle couldn't stop you, you still need to be careful.

You can't really sneak up on this creature. This creature can hear even the slightest movement...

As the Pridens say, that was one fine hunt! You can be proud of yourself - this was not just a fight with a huge cat. It's a proof that mutated animals can be killed. And that's great! Now we know that we can gain control over the Bestiary and unravel its secrets."
text

Ferris has all sorts of creatures on it. Like the Gastornis, those overgrown chickens...

Let's hear what Sergey Dozorin had to say:

"Alright, here is the deal.

They say there is a rooster in every yard in Kanian villages. To wake them up in the morning, or to keep hens happy - I'm not sure. The Bestiary has its rooster, too. It's a Gastornis, actually. A giant bird that can only be found on Ferris. It can't fly - I bet that's why it's so angry. If you live right next to creatures with a taste for bird meat, there's only one thing you can do - become the scariest beast in the neighborhood and eat everyone yourself.

Our rooster learned that lesson well. So it will try to eat you as soon as it sees you. Just because it can. You will be intruding into its territory, after all. Unfortunately, there is no way you can get around it. It picked a perfect spot.

The good news is, this specimen is the only one of its kind. A relict creature, as the Surveyors call it. If you deal with it, you won't have to worry about Gastornises ever again."

There you have it. Did you deal with it? Can some bird stop the Hero of Sarnaut? Exactly, and don't you doubt it.

"That chicken was stronger than I thought! How are you? Are you alright? Still have all your limbs? Great. Now let's explore the Bestiary."
text

So what is the Bestiary?

The Empire's secret training ground where they performed experiments on various local animals. The key part of these experiments was an object that was found in that very lake, enclosed in a piece of a meteorite. The Imperials used it on test subjects with varying degrees of success. As you can see, that worm, the "Specimen", managed to escape in the end. It settled somewhere around here.

Meanwhile, the local animals started to suffer from some kind of disease. They began to turn into "modificants". Do you remember the Blight? Wait, it's not that simple!

I'll remind you about something else - on the Eclipse, when you fought Captain Krivov, his construct turned into some kind of creature that emanated the air of "order", right? Does anything here seem familiar to you?

Okay, let’s get back to business. Finding an entrance to the Bestiary was not easy. You were lucky. This is how Herbert put it:

"One of our jaegers, Sergey Dozorin, sent me a message yesterday. He has found another entrance to the Bestiary. He has somehow activated a Portal in a cave in the Deadly Frostland. The Tungars use that cave it for their pagan rituals. And we have both seen what Tungar gods are capable of...

I don't think you will be able to get past them undetected like Dozorin did, but you can always fight your way through. Maas-Tyna the Light-Footed in our first camp can show you the way.

The Bestiary might have answers to many of our questions, so we can't miss this opportunity to find them."

I can keep up with it, even on my rusty prostheses. I think Tep was supposed to come in the past millennia. Or the next one? I don't remember."

"Here he is. Speak of the devil, hahahahaha!! He's been lying in the coffin for ages... I asked if he wanted to shower - we have a bathroom in the back. He looked at me like I was an idiot. That damned egghead. And his Mechanoids are ugly, though they were based on my schematics. And he himself looks... wrong. The Source is more beautiful. The Source told me that Tep is just a drop in the ocean. That Tep is useless. I should kick Tep out. He has no business being here. Get out!"

 "Everything is smoking and shaking! I think Tep is angry. I never thought he could scream like that. For a moment, I was genuinely afraid. Maybe he was practicing? I need to practice, too (will start tomorrow after lunch). The bad news is that the Source wasn't able to resist him. If it hadn't been for my Mechanoids, I'd be dead right now. So what should you say? Thank you, Negus Jeeg. It's a good thing you exist."

After reading the journal, Herbert realized a few things:

Whatever the answers to these questions are, we probably won't like them. I'm starting to wonder if it might be better for us to forget about Ferris, like the Empire did once."

Oh, that Negus Jeeg of yours is a terrifying one. I've never liked madmen, but this Arisen is something else.

What can one say about a maniac's motives? You never know what's going on in their head. That's why they are so dangerous.

Herbert understood that as well as I do.

I will show you the way... Hurry, before he strikes! Be careful - we don't know what to expect from him. There is nothing more dangerous than a mad fanatic! He's been surviving here on his own all this time. I wonder how...

I hope it was the real Jeeg you took down. That it was the original, and not a copy. That this maniac is not hiding somewhere in the complex...

As you can see, the Mechanoids were originally created by this psychopath. He's quite a skilled one. Lots of the things he created are still operational to this day. But his most successful invention is the security system of the Central Laboratory. And now it has also been "modified" and upgraded!

This is what Herbert said:

"As you already know, this place is mostly guarded by the Mechanoids. They do it pretty well - the scientists are long gone, and they are still protecting the complex! But what if the Mechanoids had been affected by the "modifying crystal" back then? Would they have continued following the orders, or would they have turned against their owners? It's a tricky question, and we will have to answer it.

Modified Mechanoids that guard the laboratory are blocking our way. I have no idea what they are capable of. This technology is far more advanced than anything the Elves or the ZIT Headquarters could have come up with. I wish we didn't have to destroy it.

Come back as soon as you're done with them. We'll decide what to do next.

The design of the robots suggests they were meant to operate in pairs. Though occasionally they fire on each other."

You managed to defeat the machines.

t: text

When the expedition was over, the heroes received Zayan's letter.

"Good day!

First of all, let me congratulate you on surviving the battle with the Architects.

It is my duty to inform you that we have studied the cloning system and found answers to all our questions. You may find it interesting that this technology was initially developed on Ferris without the use of any otherworldly materials. The Object - or the Sculptor - provided the energy source for this miracle of engineering. That is why all clones, including pseudo-Herbert and pseudo-Elena, turned into modificants so quickly. Their high intelligence shows that the process of creating a living being from scratch went smoothly. However, the Sculptor's influence on the staff turned to be rather damaging.

Most likely, Tep had learned about the cloning technology and the principles of matter and energy manipulation during his visit to Ferris.

Sarn, the "Master" of the cultists, took high interest in the activities of Tep and his minions. This is how the cloning technology got into the hands of the cultist leader, Gorluxor. Comparing their cloning systems proves our theory true.

Well, this is it. Thank you for all your efforts in keeping our expedition safe. Murk is looking forward to another adventure like that one. He said, and I quote: "If you don't call me next time you fight these hunhurrs, you will regret it!"

Yours respectfully,

Zayan.

P.S.: Herbert and Elena have departed together to an unknown location. I know we probably won't see them in the League or the Empire again. Still, if you meet them again some day, tell them they are always welcome here."
text

This is how Marianne reacted:

"Well, so that happened. I could blame the Sculptor for his treachery, but what's the point? Obviously, we shouldn't have trusted him from the very beginning. He is too different from us.

I must admit I was hoping that, knowing what it's like to be completely alone, he wouldn't turn his back on us. But everyone makes mistakes, and I'm not an exception."

I suppose we are done here. Don't let the Sculptor's actions overshadow your triumph! You have accomplished a great feat. One of your greatest, probably.

I hope our victory puts an end to this story. I will hope and pray for this... Every day! Can the Architects return now that we have destroyed the Path? I'm afraid nobody knows that. So there is no point in worrying.

I have to decide what to do with the Historians and Ferris. The Empire's presence makes things more complicated. I don't think they are eager to share their secrets. However, I can handle this. You should go see Aidenus as soon as possible. He's the one who can tell us what to do."

This is how Aidenus summed it up:

"So that's how that happened. The Cataclysm taught us nothing! We continue to toy with forces that are beyond our understanding! First Nezeb with his vain efforts, and now Zayan with his endless search for knowledge... Ah, at least this time it ended well.

So... The Architects, uninvited guests from the beyond. As Tensess said, the universe only gives you what you can handle. This time these creatures met with a rebuff. If they come again, we will handle them one way or another. Would they dare to? We will keep an eye out for them! The Empire is not vain, so we'll crush them and be done with it!

I thank you for your great deed! You saved not only the League, but the entire Sarnaut. You cannot imagine how proud I am to have a hero like you in our ranks!"

The battle with Locus was extremely difficult. But eventually he was defeated.

The harmony is gone... The Order is broken... Locus... Is no longer needed..." the Architect's voce said.

"To become perfect, you say?" Rysina said, crushing one of the Architect's cores. "Oops, I've stepped on your perfection! Hey, what's happening?"

"Locus is self-destructing! Run!" Marianne yelled.

"Move, move!" you all ran out of the center of the Order.

Locus fell apart...

"Oh... may the Light save us. Now that everything's over..." Marianne stopped to catch a breath.

"Nothing is over. Look around you!" As soon as you turned around, you saw a horde of Locuses that kept coming.

"Great Tensess..." Marianne managed to say.

Rysina was furious:

"Unbelievable... That thing! You tricked us! Lured us into a trap! We will destroy you! Destroy all of you, one after another!"

"Funny. If you destroy me, you will destroy your way home. I have fulfilled our agreement. You disrupted the Path, but you cannot defeat the Architect. Leave. Go back. Remember, children of chaos: the Order cannot be changed!" With those words, the Sculptor vanished.
